[An<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />drew his Brother] Simon Peters</ns0:hi> Brother, by <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> directed to Christ, <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 1.40. called by Christ together with his Bro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther <ns0:hi>Peter, Mar.</ns0:hi> 1.16. <ns0:hi>Iames the Son of Zebedee</ns0:hi> so called, to distinguish him from another of the Apostles of the same Name, who was the Son of <ns0:hi>Alpheus.</ns0:hi> This is he of whose Death we read, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 12.2. he was slain by <ns0:hi>Herod,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iohn his Brother, viz.</ns0:hi> the Son of <ns0:hi>Alpheus</ns0:hi>; this is he who was called the <ns0:hi>Beloved Disciple,</ns0:hi> who also wro te the Gospel of <ns0:hi>Iohn, Iohn</ns0:hi> 1.20. [<ns0:hi>Philip</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Bartholomew</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Thomas.</ns0:hi>] <ns0:hi>Philip</ns0:hi> was of <ns0:hi>Bethsaida,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>City of Andrew</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Peter, Iohn</ns0:hi> 1.44. found and called by Christ, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 43. of the Call of <ns0:hi>Bartho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lomew</ns0:hi> we do not read, some think him the same with <ns0:hi>Natha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />niel</ns0:hi> mentioned, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 1.45, 46. <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> It is some inducement to believe it, that he is here Named with <ns0:hi>Philip,</ns0:hi> who was the instrument to bring him to Christ, <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 1.45. but there is nothing of this certain. <ns0:hi>Thomas,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>same</ns0:hi> who was called <ns0:hi>Didymus,</ns0:hi> who was so unbelieving as to Christ's Resurrection, <ns0:hi>Iohn,</ns0:hi> 20.24.27. and <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Publicane,</ns0:hi> he that wrote this History of the Gospel, we heard before of his <ns0:hi>Call</ns0:hi> from the receit of Custom, he was also called <ns0:hi>Levi. Iames the Son of Alpheus,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Lebbeus, whose surname was Thaddeus.</ns0:hi> This <ns0:hi>Iames</ns0:hi> is call'd <ns0:hi>Iames</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>lesser, Mark</ns0:hi> 15.40. and so distinguished from <ns0:hi>Iames</ns0:hi> the Son of <ns0:hi>Zebedee.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Brother of our Lord, Gal.</ns0:hi> 1.19. (that is as some think his Kinsman) judging him not the Son of <ns0:hi>Alpheus,</ns0:hi> who was the Father of <ns0:hi>Matthew,</ns0:hi> but another <ns0:hi>Alpheus</ns0:hi> the Husband of <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> the Wife of <ns0:hi>Cleopas, Ioh.</ns0:hi> 19.25. But this appeareth not from Scripture. In stead of <ns0:hi>Lebbeus,</ns0:hi> whose Surname was <ns0:hi>Thad<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />deus, Luke</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 6.16. <ns0:hi>Iudas</ns0:hi> the Brother of <ns0:hi>Iames</ns0:hi> (he that wrote the Epistle of <ns0:hi>Iude,</ns0:hi> as appeareth by <ns0:hi>Iude.</ns0:hi>) <ns0:hi>Mark Ch.</ns0:hi> 3.17. mentions not <ns0:hi>Lebbeus</ns0:hi> at all, which makes some think that the Words are Transposed, and should be <ns0:hi>Thaddeus</ns0:hi> the Son of <ns0:hi>Lebbeus</ns0:hi>; for <ns0:hi>Thaddai</ns0:hi> in the <ns0:hi>Syriack</ns0:hi> is the same with <ns0:hi>Iudas. Simon</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Canaanite, Luke</ns0:hi> calls him <ns0:hi>Simon Zelotes, Luke</ns0:hi> 6.15. <ns0:hi>& Acts</ns0:hi> 1.13; we must not un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />derstand by <ns0:hi>Canaanite</ns0:hi> a Pagan (for Christ sent out none but <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi>) but one of <ns0:hi>Cana,</ns0:hi> which by Interpretation is <ns0:hi>Zelus,</ns0:hi> from whence it is that <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> calleth him <ns0:hi>Zelotes.</ns0:hi> [And <ns0:hi>Iudas Iscariot who also betrayed him.</ns0:hi>] There are many guesses, how <ns0:hi>Iudas</ns0:hi> had the Name of <ns0:hi>Iscariot</ns0:hi>; whether from <ns0:hi>Kerioth,</ns0:hi> sup<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />posed to be his Town, or on some other account, the gues<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ses of the best are but incertainties, nor is it material for us to know. It here distinguisheth him from the other <ns0:hi>Iudas.</ns0:hi> Of his betraying his Master, we shall hear afterward. Christ al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tered the Names of <ns0:hi>Simon,</ns0:hi> whom he called <ns0:hi>Peter, Mark</ns0:hi> 3.16. He added to the Names of <ns0:hi>Iames and Iohn,</ns0:hi> calling them <ns0:hi>Beanerges,</ns0:hi> that is, the <ns0:hi>Sons of Thunder, v.</ns0:hi> 17. <ns0:hi>Thaddeus</ns0:hi> is cal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />led <ns0:hi>Iudas,</ns0:hi> and by <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> also <ns0:hi>Lebbeus.</ns0:hi> These were the 12 first Apostles, to which were added (after Christ's Ascen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sion) <ns0:hi>Matthias</ns0:hi> (in stead of <ns0:hi>Iudas Iscariot) Paul</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Bar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nabas,</ns0:hi> but these conversed with Christ, and were the first sent out by him. We shall now hear the Instruction he gives them.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:234" />5. These twelve Jesus sent forth, and comman<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ded them, saying, Go not into the way of theGen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tiles, and into <ns0:hi>any</ns0:hi> city of the Samaritanes enter ye not.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">6 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Cha. 15.24</ns0:note> But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.<ns0:note place="bottom">Here Christ limiteth their Ministry to the Jews. The A<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />postle tells us, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 15.8. <ns0:hi>Christ was the Minister of the Circumcision, for the truth of God to Confirm the Promises made to the Fathers,</ns0:hi> and the Apostle tells the Jews, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 13.46. <ns0:hi>That it was necessary, that the Word of God should be first spoken to them.</ns0:hi> Therefore in this his first Mission, he re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />strains his Apostles from going to the Gentiles<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> to whom they had afterwards a <ns0:hi>Commission</ns0:hi> to go, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 28.19. and did go, but not before the Jews had Judged themselves unworthy of everlasting Life, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 13.46. by rejecting, and blaspheming the Gospel, and persecuting the Ministers of it; They are also commanded not to go into any City of the <ns0:hi>Samaritanes.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Samaritanes</ns0:hi> were partly Jews Apostatized, and partly Heathens, descended from those whom the <ns0:hi>King</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Syria</ns0:hi> se<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t thither, when the Ten Tribes were carried into Captivity, 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 17.6. and from some <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> left in the Land. You shall read of their Religion there, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 31. to the end. They were perfectly hated by the Jews, and as perfect H<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ters of them, as may be gathered from <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 9.52.53, <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 4.9. Our Lord, partly in regard they also were no better than Gentiles, and so ha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ted as they were of the Jews, would not suffer these his fir<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t Ministers to go, and preach amongst them. Not that they were forbidden (if some particular Persons, whether Gen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tiles or <ns0:hi>Samaritanes</ns0:hi> came to them,) to Preach to them, but on<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly not to make it their Work to go into their Country, or Ci<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ties; the time was not yet come for this great Light to shine upon the Gentiles. <ns0:hi>But go rather to the l<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>st sheep of the house of Israel.</ns0:hi> By <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> he here meaneth the two Tribes that c<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ave to the House of <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> for the 10 Tribes ever since their Captivity, 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 17.6. had lo<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t their share in that Name. He cal<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> them <ns0:hi>lost sheep,</ns0:hi> in the Sense that <ns0:hi>Ieremy</ns0:hi> speaks, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 50.6. <ns0:hi>My People have been lost Sheep; their Shepherds have caused them to go astray.</ns0:hi> So that <ns0:hi>lost Sheep</ns0:hi> here signifies <ns0:hi>wandring Sheep,</ns0:hi> for want of proper Guides. The Jews at this time, had Miserable Teachers, so as they wandred as <ns0:hi>lost Sheep,</ns0:hi> and this Comporteth with what we had in the last Ver<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ses of the former <ns0:hi>Chapter.</ns0:hi> There was a great Harvest, and but few Labourers, he is therefore providing them Labourers, Shepherds that should gather those scattered Sheep into one Fold.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">7 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luke 9.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> And as ye go, preach, saying, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ch 3.2 <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 4 17.</ns0:note> The king<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dom of heaven is at hand.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out devils, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Acts 3.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 20.</ns0:note> freely ye have received, free<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly give.<ns0:note place="bottom">In these Words he gives them Power, 1. <ns0:hi>To Preach the Gospel.</ns0:hi> 2. <ns0:hi>To confirm the Doctrine they preached to be of God, by Miraculous Operations.</ns0:hi> Healing the sick, cleansing Lepers, casting out Devils He bids them go Preach <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. <ns0:hi>Cry like Heralds,</ns0:hi> something like <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi>'s Commission, <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> 58.1. <ns0:hi>Cry aloud, spare not, lift up thy Voice, lift up thy Voice like a Trumpet.</ns0:hi> He teacheth them what should be the Sum of their Sermons. <ns0:hi>The Kingdom of God</ns0:hi> is <ns0:hi>at Hand,</ns0:hi> the same thing which <ns0:hi>Iohn Baptist</ns0:hi> preached, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 3. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 2. which Christ Preached, <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 1.15. and which he directed the 70 to Preach, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 10.9. not that they were to use no o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther Words, but that all the Words they used, were to have this Tendency, To declare that the time was now come, when God had fulfilled his promise of the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> who was setting up his Kingdom in the World, and to whose Laws they were to be obedient. This Doctrine they were to confirm by <ns0:hi>Miracles.</ns0:hi> Which he gives them a charge, they should work <ns0:hi>freely</ns0:hi> without receiving any reward for them, that the Mira<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cles being used to their private Profit, might not lose their end, which was the Confirmation of their Doctrine.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 Provide <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luke 9.3. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 10.4</ns0:note> neither gold, nor silver, nor brass in your purses.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 Nor scrip for your journey, neither two coats, neither shoes, nor yet staves. <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luke 12<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 1 Tim. 5.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> For the work<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />man is worthy of his meat.<ns0:note place="bottom">Our Saviour having in the last Verse commanded them to give freely, they might reasonably be thinking, that they had need to provide well for their Journey. No, saith our Saviour, <ns0:hi>Provide neither Gold, nor Silver, nor Brass, &c.</ns0:hi> That this was but a Temporary Precept, the Will of God concerning them for this short Journey, appeareth from <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 22.35, 36. <ns0:hi>But now he that hath a Purse, let him take it, and like<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />wise his Scrip,</ns0:hi> &c. They were to finish this Journey in a short time, and much Provision would have been an hindrance to their Motion. Besides our Saviour designed to give them an ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />perience of the <ns0:hi>Providence of God,</ns0:hi> and to teach them to trust in it, as also to teach People, <ns0:hi>That the Labourer is worthy of his Hire,</ns0:hi> and that God expecteth, that his Ministers should not live of their own, but upon the Altar which they served, so as at once he taught his Apostles not to be Covetous, nor over<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />much Sollicitous, and People to provide for those who Ministred to them in things Spiritual. I pass over what others have Cri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tically observed concerning the Words, that being not my pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />per Work. <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 6.8. <ns0:hi>That he commanded them that they should take nothing for their Iourney, save a Staff only, no Scrip, no Bread, nor Money in their Purse, but be shod with Sandals, and not put on two Coats.</ns0:hi> From whence is plain that the Staves forbidden in <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> were ei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther <ns0:hi>Staves</ns0:hi> for <ns0:hi>defence,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>to bear Burdens</ns0:hi> upon, not meer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly <ns0:hi>Travellers Staves.</ns0:hi> The Sum is, in this their first Journey, which they were soon to dispatch, he would have them trust God, for <ns0:hi>Protection,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Sustenance,</ns0:hi> and load themselves with nothing more than necessary.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:234" />11 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk. 10.8.</ns0:note> And into whatsoever city or town ye shall enter, enquire who in it is worthy, and there abide, till ye go thence.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 And when ye come into an house, salute it.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 And if the house be worthy let your peace come upon it, but if it be not worthy, let your peace return to you.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 And. <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk. 9.5. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 10.10. Acts 10.6.</ns0:note> whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, when ye depart out of that house, or city, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk. 9.5. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 10.10. Acts 10.6.</ns0:note> shake off the dust of your feet.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 Verily I say unto you, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 11, 22.24<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                  </ns0:note> It shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah, in the day of judgment, then for that city.<ns0:note place="bottom">Our Lord had before set them their Limits, and appointed them their works, and directed them as to their Accou<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />trements for their Journey, here he directeth them their Me<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thods. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> hath much of the same instructions, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 10. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 4, 5, 6. but applyed to the seventy, not to the twelve. <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> hath something of them applyed to the twelve, <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 6.10, 11. <ns0:hi>And he said unto them, In what place soever you en<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter into an House, there abide until you depart from that place; and whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear you, when you depart thence, shake off the dust under your Feet, for a Testimony against them. Verily I say vnto you, it shall be more tolerable for</ns0:hi> Sodom <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> Gomorrah <ns0:hi>in the day of Iudg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment, than for that City.</ns0:hi> The method Christ set them was, when they came into any of the Cities of <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> to inquire if there were any <ns0:hi>worthy</ns0:hi> Persons in it, and thither to go, and there to abide (if they did not find they were mistaken) untill they left that place; and when they came into an House to <ns0:hi>salute it,</ns0:hi> wishing all<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                     <ns0:hi>Peace</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Happiness</ns0:hi> to it, if they found themselves Welcome, to Preach to it the Gospel of Peace. But if they found themselves unwelcome, and discerned, that the People of the City, or of that House, did not care for their Company, and refused to hear them, they should not make themselves, or the Gospel a burden to them, but shew their Contempt of those who contemned the Gospel, and the Ministry of it, by <ns0:hi>shaking the dust off their Feet, as a Testimony against them.</ns0:hi> Then he con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cludes telling them, That the Lord would so grievously at last revenge such Contempt, that the Condition of the Men of <ns0:hi>Sodom and Gomorrah,</ns0:hi> who were destroyed by Fire and <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>rimstone, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 19.24. would at the last day be more to<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lerable than theirs. This is the Sum, by which our Saviour doth obviate the sollicitous Thoughts, might from his for<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mer words arise in their Minds. How shall we live, going amongst Strangers, if we carry nothing with us? Saith our Saviour, when you first come into a Town or City, do not inquire for the Inns that entertain Strangers, but who is <ns0:hi>Wor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thy, Worthy</ns0:hi> of such Guests, so <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 11.38. A <ns0:hi>Son of Peace, Luk.</ns0:hi> 10.6. who are accounted, as the most Pious, and Reli<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gious Persons in that Town or City, or best affected to the Gospel, (he hereby hints, that <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Baptist</ns0:hi> and his Ministry had had such Success, that in most places there were some such Persons.) <ns0:hi>Worthy,</ns0:hi> doth not in our ordinary Dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />course signifie always a <ns0:hi>meritorious Person,</ns0:hi> but a Person <ns0:hi>Ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />celling,</ns0:hi> either, in <ns0:hi>Religion</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Knowledge,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Moral Vertue.</ns0:hi> Such Persons our Lord presumes would entertain those, who came upon so kind an Errand, to their Houses, he Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mands them to go, and when they came to an House to sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lute it: To say, <ns0:hi>Peace be to this House</ns0:hi> (which was the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> ordinary Salutation) under the Notion of <ns0:hi>Peace</ns0:hi> they com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />prehended all Good. But, <ns0:hi>Let your Peace be upon it</ns0:hi> (I conceive) comprehendeth more, viz. <ns0:hi>Preach the Gospel of Peace unto it</ns0:hi>: Or, my <ns0:hi>Peace</ns0:hi> shall be upon it. I will bless that House. But if you find you are mis-informed, or mistaken, <ns0:hi>your Peace shall return unto you</ns0:hi>; you have done your Work, and you shall have your reward. <ns0:hi>If they will not receive you, nor hear your Words.</ns0:hi> If they declare any Contempt of you, and will not hear the glad Tidings of the Gospel: <ns0:hi>When you depart out of that House or City, shake off the dust of your Feet.</ns0:hi> This was more than a sign of Contempt of them, we read of <ns0:hi>Nehemiah ch.</ns0:hi> 5.13. that he <ns0:hi>shook his Lap,</ns0:hi> and said<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                     <ns0:hi>so God shake out every Man from his House, and from his Labour that performeth not this Promise</ns0:hi>: We have but one Instance of this Practice of the <ns0:hi>Apostles, Acts</ns0:hi> 13.51. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> adds for a <ns0:hi>Testimony against them.</ns0:hi> A Testimony of Gods despising them, who despised his Grace, and of the Vengeance of God, that should come upon them for that Contempt. For he adds, <ns0:hi>It shall be more tolerable for</ns0:hi> Sodom <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> Gomorrah <ns0:hi>in the day of Iudgment,</ns0:hi> the last Judgment, <ns0:hi>than for that City.</ns0:hi> Their Condemnation will be more dreadful, as having sinned against greater Light, and fairer offers of greater Grace than ever they had.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk. 10.3.</ns0:note> Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rom. 16.19.</ns0:note> he ye therefore wise as ser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pents, and <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>simple.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> harmless as doves.<ns0:note place="bottom">Our Lord having hitherto instructed his twelve Apostles, as to the places whither they were to go, the work they had to do, and the Methods, he would have them observe, now comes to arm them against their Difficulties, and the Temptations they were like to meet with. <ns0:hi>I send you forth</ns0:hi> (saith he) <ns0:hi>as Sheep amongst Wolves.</ns0:hi> It is most probable, that our Saviour speaks this with refe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rence to what they were like to meet with, when he should be taken from them, for we do not read of any great op<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />position, which they at present met with. I send you, saith he, <ns0:hi>as Sheep</ns0:hi> which are feeble Creatures in themselves, and without any natural Armour to defend themselves, <ns0:hi>amongst Wolves,</ns0:hi> which are rapacious Creatures, and have a particular Enmity to Sheep. Amongst Enemies who will have as great an inclination from their Malice to devour you, as Wolves have from their Nature) to devour Sheep. <ns0:hi>Be you there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore Wise as Serpents.</ns0:hi> It is said of the Serpent, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 3.1. that <ns0:hi>he was more subtil than any Beast of the Field.</ns0:hi> Na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />turalists observe, yet, a great natural<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> Sagacity in the <ns0:hi>Ser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pent,</ns0:hi> which they note in several particulars: It is hard to say, that Christ aimed at this, or that particular thing, wherein the Sagacity of Serpents appeareth. He only pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />poseth the Serpent, as a Pattern of Subtilty, and commend<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth Prudence to them, so far as it consisteth with <ns0:hi>Inno<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cency,</ns0:hi> for it followeth, <ns0:hi>Innocent</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Doves.</ns0:hi> Amongst the Beasts of the Field, there is none more innocent than a <ns0:hi>Sheep.</ns0:hi> Amongst the Birds of the Air, none more inno<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cent than a <ns0:hi>Dove,</ns0:hi> to both these, our Lord compareth his Dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ciples. This Text teacheth us, 1. That <ns0:hi>Wisdome</ns0:hi> may dwell with Prudence. 2. That all <ns0:hi>true Prudence</ns0:hi> must be at<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tended with <ns0:hi>Innocency.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 But beware of men, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 24.9. Mar. 13.9. Luk. 21.12.</ns0:note> for they will deli<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ver you up to the councils, and they will scourge you in their synagogues.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Acts. 5.40. Acts 12.1. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 25.23.</ns0:note> ye shall be brought before gover<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nours and kings for my sake, for a testimony against them and the gentiles<ns0:note place="bottom">The last word <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> maketh it plain, that our blessed Lord is not here arming his Disciples so much against any opposition they were like to meet with upon this their first going out, for they were not to go to the <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> as those they should meet with some years after his Ascension; yet not excluding what they should meet with from the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> for what is said, about delivering up to the <ns0:hi>Councils</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Scourging in the Synagogues,</ns0:hi> seemeth to have a particular reference to the <ns0:hi>Iews.</ns0:hi> This Scripture was most eminently fulfilled, as to the Apostles, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 4.1, 2, 3. <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> 5.27. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 6.12. and as to being brought before <ns0:hi>Governours</ns0:hi> and Kings, there are instances enough in the <ns0:hi>Acts,</ns0:hi> more in <ns0:hi>Ecclesiastical stories.</ns0:hi> Neither do I think our Saviour hath in these words any re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ference to the distinction of their <ns0:hi>Councils</ns0:hi> amongst the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi>; he only designed to let them know, the time would come, when for their owning him, and Preaching his Gospel, they should be brought before all sorts of <ns0:hi>Magistrates,</ns0:hi> and in all kinds of Courts. That Phrase [<ns0:hi>and they will scourge you in their Synagogues</ns0:hi>] hath mightily perplexed some, especially such as have dreamed <ns0:hi>Religious Synagogues</ns0:hi> too Holy places for such Offices, but there is no need that we should take the term <ns0:hi>Synagogues</ns0:hi> here for the <ns0:hi>Places of their Worship,</ns0:hi> it doth as well signifie <ns0:hi>in their Conventions,</ns0:hi> and there are some that think, that they had adjoyning to their <ns0:hi>Synagogues,</ns0:hi> a place in which they punished Offenders, upon the Account of <ns0:hi>Religion</ns0:hi>; certain it is, 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 11.24. That <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> was five times <ns0:hi>Scourged</ns0:hi> by the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> according to their Law, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 25.3. <ns0:hi>for a Testimony against them, and the</ns0:hi> Gentiles. A Testimony for me, that is expressed in those words, <ns0:hi>for my Names sake,</ns0:hi> and against them, whether <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi>: A <ns0:hi>Testimony</ns0:hi> against them in the day of Judgment. <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, hence our terms of <ns0:hi>Martyr</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Martyrdom,</ns0:hi> the one signifies a Witness, the other a Testimony.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk. 21.14.</ns0:note> But when they deliver you up, take no thought how, or what ye shall speak: for it shall be given you in that same hour, what ye shall speak.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 For it is not ye that speak, but the spi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rit of your Father which speaketh in you.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> hath much the same, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 13.11. so hath <ns0:hi>Luke. ch.</ns0:hi> 12.11, 12. The Apostles being Men but of an ordinary Education, before Christ called them, he might reasonably suppose, that they would not appear before <ns0:hi>Councils,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Kings,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Governours</ns0:hi> without some Abashment, having not been accustomed to such Presences; he therefore arms them in these words, wherein he doth not prohibit ordi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nary Thoughts, which every man hath before he speaketh, but anxious Thoughts aforehand, for saith he, <ns0:hi>it shall be gi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven you in that hour, what you shall speak.</ns0:hi> The Lord seemeth to speak here, as he did to <ns0:hi>Moses, Exod.</ns0:hi> 4.12. complaining he was of a <ns0:hi>slow Speech, and of a slow Tongue,</ns0:hi> v. 11. <ns0:hi>Who hath made Mans mouth?</ns0:hi> It shall, saith Christ, <ns0:hi>be given you</ns0:hi> from God. <ns0:hi>For it is not you that speak, but the Spirit of your Father which speaketh in you</ns0:hi>: That is, not you, from your selves only: The Holy Spirit shall in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fluence your Thoughts as to the <ns0:hi>Matter,</ns0:hi> and suggest that to you, and it shall in<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>luence your Tongues, giving you a <ns0:hi>Free<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dom</ns0:hi> of Speech. This was verified in <ns0:hi>Stephen, Acts</ns0:hi> 6.10. and hath been eminently verified in a multitude of <ns0:hi>Martyrs,</ns0:hi> We may observe from hence, That the influence of the Spi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rit is not to be confined to the Will and <ns0:hi>Affections.</ns0:hi> It hath also an influence upon our words in the Service of God; not that we can conclude, that whatsoever Christians so speak, either, in their <ns0:hi>Confessions</ns0:hi> or other <ns0:hi>Duties,</ns0:hi> is from such immediate Assistance, but there is such an influence, tho the Spirit in this, as in other Operations, like the wind bloweth where and when it listeth.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:235" />21 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mic. 7.6.</ns0:note> And the brother shall deliver up the brother to death, and the father the child, and the children shall rise up against <ns0:hi>their</ns0:hi> parents, and cause them to be put to death.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 And ye shall be hated of all men for my Names sake, but <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 24.13.</ns0:note> he that endureth to the end shall be saved.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> speaketh much the same, tho as spoken upon ano<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther occasion, <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 21.16, 17. Our Saviour here tells them, that the Persecutions would reach even to Death it self, and that the Malice of the World against him and his Gospel should proceed so far, as to extinguish all natural affection, betwixt Brethren, and Parents, and Children, and that they would meet with a multitude of Enemies (for that is here meant by <ns0:hi>All,</ns0:hi> not every individual man, as in a multitude of other Scriptures.) The Root of all Persecution is <ns0:hi>Hatred. For my Names sake,</ns0:hi> for Preaching or Professing of my Gospel, and living up to the Rule of it, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 4.18. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 5.41. This is that which <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> calleth <ns0:hi>suffering as a Christian,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 4.16. And by this Phrase, he doth not only admonish them of their Duty, to see that they suffered <ns0:hi>for his Names sake,</ns0:hi> but also incourage them from the Honourable cause of their suffering, it was for his Names sake. He also addeth an<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />other Argument, <ns0:hi>But he that indureth to the end shall be saved.</ns0:hi> There shall be an end of these Sufferings, if they end not in your Life-time, they will end with your Lives, and if you continue to the end, you shall be saved. It is neither true Patience, nor will it be profitable, if it holdeth not out to the end, <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 13.13. 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 9.24. <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 3.6.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 2.13. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 4.12. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 12.75. Act. 8.1. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 9.25. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 14.6.</ns0:note> But when they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another: For verily I say unto you, Ye shall not have <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                     <ns0:hi>Finished.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> gone over the cities of Israel, until the Son of man be come.<ns0:note place="bottom">Whether this Text at all warranteth Ministers flight in a time of Persecution I doubt, it seemeth to be a <ns0:hi>special Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mand</ns0:hi> given to the Apostles, that they might have a time be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore the coming of Christ here spoken of, to Preach the Gospel all over the Cities of <ns0:hi>Israel.</ns0:hi> But that in some Cases it is lawful to fly, I do not at all doubt, (tho I do question whether it be to be warranted from this Text) what those Cases are, is largely Discoursed, particularly by Mr. <ns0:hi>Torshell.</ns0:hi> Generally it is said, <ns0:hi>wherever</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Glory of God,</ns0:hi> Or, <ns0:hi>the good of others</ns0:hi> calls to us for such a flight<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> But what may be judg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed in such Cases, is a more particular Question. <ns0:hi>Augustine</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Honoratus</ns0:hi> speaketh well in the Case. Ministers ought not to fly rashly, nor <ns0:hi>out of Cowardise,</ns0:hi> nor that they might live elsewhere <ns0:hi>Lazily,</ns0:hi> nor when their flight will betray the Church of God. Not where the Persecution is General, but where the Persecution is particular, against some of them, and there will be enough left for the Care of the Church in their absence, and with the Consent of the Church they may fly. But this is too large a Case to be spoken to here: Especially, considering (as I said) that I do not think that any f<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ght is to be justified from this Text, the Precept being particu<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ar for special Reasons. <ns0:hi>Vntil the Son of Man come.</ns0:hi> There is a wonderful Variety of Interpreters Senses of this Text founded upon the various Comings of Christ mentioned in Holy Writ: He was already come in the Flesh, so as it speak<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing of a time to come, could not be meant of that: Nor can it be unde<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>tood of his second <ns0:hi>coming to Iudgment,</ns0:hi> for they have gone through the <ns0:hi>Cities of Israel</ns0:hi> long ago. Christ is therefore said in Scripture to <ns0:hi>come, when he appeareth in some great work of Providence,</ns0:hi> whether of <ns0:hi>Iudgment</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Mercy.</ns0:hi> This makes some interpret it of the <ns0:hi>Destruction of Ierusalem</ns0:hi>; in which Sense some think the <ns0:hi>coming of Christ</ns0:hi> is mentioned, <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 24. Some <ns0:hi>of the Resurrection of Christ,</ns0:hi> from whence they say Christ's <ns0:hi>Epocha</ns0:hi> commenced. Others understand it of the <ns0:hi>Effusion of the Spirit in the day</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Pentecost,</ns0:hi> this they ground on <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 14.17, 18. where they think Christ's <ns0:hi>coming</ns0:hi> promised, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 18. is the <ns0:hi>coming of</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Spirit</ns0:hi> promised <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 17. undoubtedly in the General, our Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viour means, <ns0:hi>till the time be accomplished, when you must leave Preaching to the Iews and go to the Gentiles,</ns0:hi> and my <ns0:hi>Kingdom</ns0:hi> shall be further extended than it is at present, which Dispensation of God, may for ought I know be call<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed the <ns0:hi>Coming of Christ</ns0:hi>; being an eminent Act of Gods <ns0:hi>Providence,</ns0:hi> by which Christ was more shewed to the World, and his Kingdom further extended.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 The disciple is not above <ns0:hi>his</ns0:hi> master, nor the servant <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Joh. 13.1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 15.20.</ns0:note> above his lord.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 It is enough for the disciple that he be as his master, and the servant as his lord: If <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 12 <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> Ma<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. 3.22. Luk. 11.13. Joh. 8.4<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> they have called the master of thehouse <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Gr. Bee<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ze<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bal.</ns0:note> Beel<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />zebub, how much more <ns0:hi>shall they call</ns0:hi> those of his houshold?<ns0:note place="bottom">As much, as if he had sad, Think not much if you meet with Persecutions: I am your Lord and Master, you are my Servants and Houshold; you have no reason to look for bet<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter measure from the World, than I your Lord meet with. It is Honour enough for you, to be used as well as I am; you know they have persecuted me, they call me <ns0:hi>Beelze<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bub,</ns0:hi> saying, that I <ns0:hi>cast out Devils by Beelzebub,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Prince of Devils.</ns0:hi> Why should you expect better? Our Saviour used the same Argument, <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 6.40. <ns0:hi>Beelzebub</ns0:hi> was the Idol of <ns0:hi>Ekron,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Kin.</ns0:hi> 1.2. The word signifies the <ns0:hi>Lord of Flyes</ns0:hi>: Either, because they invocated his help against the Flyes, or (as others say) the Name was in Derision to that Idol, given by the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> to the <ns0:hi>Prince of the Devils,</ns0:hi> because the places wherein they <ns0:hi>Sacrificed</ns0:hi> to it were infested with Flyes, which they say Gods <ns0:hi>Temple</ns0:hi> at <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> ne<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ver was, notwithstanding the multitude of Sacrifices which were there killed. Certain it is they understood by it the <ns0:hi>Prince of Devils.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 Fear them not<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> therefore: for there is no<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thing covered that shall not be revealed, and hid that shall not be known,<ns0:note place="bottom">This is a proverbial Speech used by our Saviour, upon more occasions than this, <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 4.22. <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 8.17. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 12.2. As to his present use of it, the Sense is: Tho my Gospel be now covered, and hid; yet it shall be revealed, and made known. Or, Tho your Innocency be hid, and covered, yet God shall bring forth your Judgment as the Light, and your Righte<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ousness as the Noon-day. Or, Tho your Enemies Rage and Malice be hid, and their Vengeance seemeth to sleep, yet it shall be revealed. The first seemeth most probable, from what followeth in the next Verse, which he seemeth to speak as a means to it.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">27 What I tell you in darkness, <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> speak ye in light: and what ye hear in the ear, <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> preach ye upon the house tops.<ns0:note place="bottom">The Candle of the Gospel, which God hath by <ns0:hi>Iohn the Baptist</ns0:hi> and me, lighted up, is not to be hid: Tho there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore you have it from me in private, yet do you publish it, I do as it were whisper it in your Ear by private Discourses, and in a private Converse, but it shall be made as publick, as if it were published to the greatest advantage, and do you contribute what you can unto it, do you publish my Gos<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pel, as it were upon the House tops.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">28 And fear not them which kill the body, and are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.<ns0:note place="bottom">As I told you before, you will in the Publication of my Gospel meet with opposition from men. Now that it is Preach'd as it were in Darkness, and whispered in mens Ears, there is no great noise made in the World; but the Case will be otherwise, when it cometh to be publickly revealed and published upon the house tops, but consider, the Enemies can only kill the Bodies of my Disciples: You have Souls as well as Bodies, they have no Power over your Souls, but he that hath sent you to preach, and called you to the Owning, and Profession of the Gospel, hath a Power over your Souls, as well as over your Bodies, and to punish both in <ns0:hi>Hell:</ns0:hi> We have the same, <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 12.4, 5. There is nothing so effectual to drive out of our Hearts a <ns0:hi>Slavish fear</ns0:hi> of man in the doing of our Duty, as a right apprehension of the Power of God, begetting a fear of him in our Souls.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29 Are not two sparrows sold <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                     <ns0:hi>In <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> half <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> farthing, be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing the <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> part of a R<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>
                        <ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />man <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> which see in</ns0:hi> Chap. 18.2<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> for a farthing? and one of them shall not fall on the ground with<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />out your Father.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">30 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Sam. 14 45. Luk 21.18. Acts 27.34</ns0:note> But the very hairs of your head are all numbred.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="31">31 Fear ye not therefore, ye are of more va<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lue than many sparrows.<ns0:note place="bottom">Besides consider: There is a God that governeth the World, and by his Providence influenceth, and watcheth over the most minute, and invaluable beings in it, and preserveth, and upholdeth them, it extendeth to the very Hairs of your Head, and to a <ns0:hi>Sparrow</ns0:hi> (two of which are sold ordinarily for an <ns0:hi>Assarion,</ns0:hi> the tenth part of a <ns0:hi>Roman Penny</ns0:hi>) these little Birds fall not when they are shot, without the notice of him, who is your heavenly Father, and he will much more regard even you<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> Bodies, for you are of more value than many Sparrows. Our Lord there, 1. <ns0:hi>Asserts</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vidence of God,</ns0:hi> to extend to the most minute things, to be restrained to things in Heaven, or some greater and more No<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ble Creatures. 2. <ns0:hi>He teacheth his Disciples to take courage from the Consideration of it,</ns0:hi> as being assured, that their greatest Enemies should not be able to steal, or wrest them out of Gods Hands. But if they should dye in their Testi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mony, it should be by Gods ordering.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="32">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:235" />32 Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">33 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rev. 3.5.</ns0:note> But whosoever shall deny me before men, him also will I deny before my Father which is in hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven.<ns0:note place="bottom">As this is a time for you publickly to own me, so there will be a time (in the Day of Judgment) for me to confess and publickly own you, <ns0:hi>before the Angels of God,</ns0:hi> (which <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> addeth to this Sentence, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 12.8.) as men deal with me in this Life, so I shall deal with them in that Day. Our Saviour speaketh much the same thing, as repeated by <ns0:hi>Mark Ch.</ns0:hi> 8.38. and <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 9.26. only there in stead of <ns0:hi>whosoe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ver shall deny me,</ns0:hi> it is, <ns0:hi>whosoever shall be ashamed of me, and my Words.</ns0:hi> Christ requireth of us not only a believing on him, but an <ns0:hi>External profession</ns0:hi>: nor that only, but a <ns0:hi>Confession of him,</ns0:hi> which signifyeth a profession of him, and his Gospel in the <ns0:hi>Face of Opposition</ns0:hi> and Enemies, see <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 10.10. 2. <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 2.12. It is dangerous either through <ns0:hi>shame,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>fear,</ns0:hi> to withhold our publick owning and acknowledge<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment of Christ, and his Truths, when we are called to it, much more to deny them, but the Guilt is greater, when it is through shame, for where <ns0:hi>fear</ns0:hi> is the cause, the Temptation is more high. This Text must be understood, of those who persist in such denial, for <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> denyed his Master, yet was graciously upon his Repentance received by him.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="34">34 Think not that I am come to send peace on the earth: I came not to send peace, but a sword.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="35">35 For I am come to set a man at variance against his father, and the daughter against her mother: and the daughter in-law against her mother in-law.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> hath much the same with the 34. <ns0:hi>v. Ch.</ns0:hi> 12. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 49. As the Jews were much mistaken in their notion of the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> as if he were to be a Temporal <ns0:hi>Prince,</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>restore the King<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dom to Israel,</ns0:hi> and as the <ns0:hi>Kingdom,</ns0:hi> so a peaceful Kingdom: so many Persons think still that where true <ns0:hi>Religion</ns0:hi> comes, there must be forthwith <ns0:hi>Peace</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Vnion.</ns0:hi> And indeed so it should be, and so it would be if the Gospel were Cordially, and Uni<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />versally received. It is impossible that a <ns0:hi>System of Laws</ns0:hi> should be compiled, better fitted to Humane Society, or conducea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ble to Peace, the great end of it, than the Laws of the Gos<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pel are: but <ns0:hi>Eventually</ns0:hi> it is not so, nor was such a Civil Peace the end of Christs coming. Accidentally through the Cor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ruption of mens Hearts, the Consequent of Christs coming in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to the World, and of his Gospel coming into, and prevailing in any part of the World is (as <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> phraseth it) <ns0:hi>rather di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vision,</ns0:hi> which is here called a <ns0:hi>Sword.</ns0:hi> Through mens Fondness of their Idolatry, Superstition and Lusts, and mad<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness on them, their Impatience of being outdone in Religion, and Righteousness of Conversation. The Event of Christs coming was Division, Wars, Variances, like the times Prophe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sied of by <ns0:hi>Micah. Ch.</ns0:hi> 7.6. God either stirring up Wars to revenge the Contempt of the <ns0:hi>Gospel</ns0:hi> (as it happened to the Jews) or men taking up Arms to compel all others to their Idolatries, and Superstitions. And that Natural Antipathy which men have to Holiness, setting them at Variance with those who imbracing the Gospel, love a life as becometh the Gospel of the Lord Jesus Christ, worketh so far, as Men will have no respect to their nearest Relations.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="36">36 And a <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ps. 41.9. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 55.13. Joh. 13.18.</ns0:note> mans foes <ns0:hi>shall be</ns0:hi> they of his own houshold.<ns0:note place="bottom">Not of the <ns0:hi>houshold of Faith,</ns0:hi> which sheweth that it is not the Gospel, but mens Corruptions, which causeth Division. Those who truly receive the Gospel agree well enough, at least break not out into open Feuds, but the tye of no Natu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ral or Moral Relations will hold together the Seed of the Wo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />man, and the Seed of the Serpent. This doth not always hap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pen but very ordinarily, and therefore there was need that Christ should forewarn his Disciples of it.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="37">37 He that loveth father, or mother more then me, is notworthy of me: and he that loveth son, or daughter more then me, is not worthy of me.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> seemeth to speak higher, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 14.26. <ns0:hi>If any man come to me, and hate not, his Father, and Mother, and Wife and Children, and Brethren, and Sisters, yea, and his own Life also, cannot be my Disciple.</ns0:hi> But the Sense is the same, for by <ns0:hi>hatred</ns0:hi> there is only meant <ns0:hi>Displicency,</ns0:hi> and a setting them in his esteem, below Christ, and his Commands, Christ doth not command or encourage want of Natural Affection, but only by this saying, he reduceth it to order, and shew<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth that our first Love, and Homage is due to God, and where we cannot shew what Love and Affections our <ns0:hi>Father,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Mother,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Son,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Daughter</ns0:hi> call for, without failing in that Duty which we owe unto God, or Violating some Divine Precept, we must acknowledge our Heavenly Father, even by disobeying our <ns0:hi>Earthly Parents.</ns0:hi> instead of <ns0:hi>is not worthy of me, Luke</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>cannot be my Disciple,</ns0:hi> which expound<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth this Term. He is not worthy of my Favour, of the Name of my Disciple, or the Reward I intend my Disciples.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="38">38 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luke 14.27.</ns0:note> And he that taketh not his cross, and followeth after me, is not worthy of me.<ns0:note place="bottom">We have much the same, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 16.24. <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 8.34. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 9.23. It is not he that maketh not, but <ns0:hi>he that taketh not his Cross,</ns0:hi> that is, he that doth not Willingly, and Chearful<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly, and Patiently bear, and undergo those Tryals, and Af<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />flictions, and Persecutions, which God in the way of his Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vidence, shall lay upon him, and bring him into, for my sake, and my Gospel; is not worthy of the name or Reward of my Dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ciples. Our Saviour calls all such Tryals, <ns0:hi>The Cross</ns0:hi>; either with reference to the <ns0:hi>Roman</ns0:hi> last Punishment, by <ns0:hi>Crucifying</ns0:hi> or signifying what Death he should dye, and with reference to his own Cross.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="39">39 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luke 17.33.</ns0:note> He that findeth his life, shall lose it: and he that loseth his life for my sake shall find it.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Iohn Ch.</ns0:hi> 12.25. giveth us a Commentary upon these Words thus. <ns0:hi>He that loveth his Life shall lose it, and he that hateth his Life in this World, shall keep it unto Life Eternal.</ns0:hi> He in this Text is said to <ns0:hi>find his Life,</ns0:hi> who thinks that he hath found, that is, saved it, who is so much in love with his Life, that rather than he will lose it, he will lose Gods favour, deny the Lord that bought him, deny the most Fundamental Truths of the Gospel. The Man that doth thus (saith Christ) shall lose it, possibly, he shall not obtain the end he aimeth at here, but if he doth, he shall lose Eternal Life. When on the contrary, he that is Valiant for the Truth, shall sometimes be preserved, notwithstanding his Enemies rage, but if this happens not, yet he shall have <ns0:hi>Life Eternal, his Mortality shall be swallowed up in Life.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="40">40 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap 18.5.</ns0:note> He that receiveth you, receiveth me: and he that receiveth me, receiveth him that sent me.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="41">41 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Kin. 17.10 <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 18.4. 2 Kin. 4.8.</ns0:note> He that receiveth a Prophet in the name of a Prophet, shall receive a Prophets reward: and he that receiveth a righteous man in the name of a righteous man, shall receive a righteous mans reward.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="42">42 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 25.40. Mar. 9.41.</ns0:note> And whosoever shall give to drink to one of these little ones a cup of cold water on<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly, in the name of a disciple, verily I say unto you, he shall in no wise lose his reward.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>He that receiveth you, receiveth me,</ns0:hi> &c. we have the same <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 10.16. only there it is. <ns0:hi>He that heareth you, heareth me,</ns0:hi> and there is added, <ns0:hi>And he that despiseth you, despiseth me, and he that despiseth me, despiseth him that sent me</ns0:hi>; in <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 13, 20. it is, <ns0:hi>Verily, Verily, I say unto you, he that re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceiveth whomsoever I send, receiveth me, and he that re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceiveth me, receiveth him that sent me.</ns0:hi> As great Princes account what Favour is shewn to their Embassadours, who re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />present their Persons, shewn unto themselves, and whatsoever Indignities, or Affronts are done unto them, as done to them<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />selves, so doth Christ. <ns0:hi>Receiving</ns0:hi> is a general Term, and capable of a large interpretation. That <ns0:hi>Hearing</ns0:hi> is one Branch of it, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> tells us. The Scope of the Context, and the Words that follow, do manifest that a <ns0:hi>giving Entertainment to them in their houses,</ns0:hi> is another thing here meant. There is another more inward, <ns0:hi>receiving</ns0:hi> of their <ns0:hi>Doctrine</ns0:hi> by <ns0:hi>Faith,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Love</ns0:hi> to which undoubtedly, there will be a great reward. But whether it be here intended, I doubt. Our Saviour was sending the 12 out, he had commanded them to take with them, no <ns0:hi>Gold, Silver,</ns0:hi> nor <ns0:hi>Brass,</ns0:hi> no <ns0:hi>Scrip, &c.</ns0:hi> but when they came into any City, to inquire who there were in that Ci<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ty, who were worthy Men, Favourers to the Gospel, and rea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dy to entertain Strangers, and to go to their House or Houses, Saluting them, and to abide there, till they left the place. He furnisheth them here as it were with a <ns0:hi>Ticket,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Bill of Ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />change.</ns0:hi> He gives them an Assurance, that whatsoever kind<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness should be done to them, he would account it as done to himself. And further hath assured both them, and all the World, That if any should come to them to reveal the Will of God (for that the Term <ns0:hi>Prophet</ns0:hi> signifyeth) if they give him an Entertainment upon that account, they should be re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />warded. What is here meant by the Term; a <ns0:hi>Prophets re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ward</ns0:hi> is variously guessed, whether it be. 1. The reward which God hath appointed for such as entertain his Prophets. 2. Or such a reward as such a Prophet shall himself receive, or. 3. The reward which the Prophet will give him or them, <ns0:hi>viz. Prayers</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Instruction.</ns0:hi> That which appears to me most probable, is that no more is meant, then a <ns0:hi>Liberal reward.</ns0:hi> For such shall be the reward of those who turn many to <ns0:hi>Righ<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />teousness, Dan.</ns0:hi> 12.3. Those words [<ns0:hi>in the Name of a Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phet</ns0:hi>] are both exclusive of t ose from the benefit of this pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mise<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> who receive and entertain the Ministers of the Gospel, upon any other account then this, that they are the Lords <ns0:hi>Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phets</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and also encouraging to those who may discern, they have been mistaken in their Acts of Charity of this Nature; if they have been sincere in their Designs, and Actions, they shall not lose their reward, tho the pretended <ns0:hi>Prophet</ns0:hi> so en<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tertained prove but an <ns0:hi>Impostor. And whosoever shall give to one of these little ones a Cup of Cold Water only, in the Name of a Disciple: He shall not lose his reward.</ns0:hi> Christ will not only reward those who shew love to his <ns0:hi>Prophets,</ns0:hi> but those who shew kindness to his <ns0:hi>Members,</ns0:hi> whom the World counts Contemptible, and calleth <ns0:hi>little ones</ns0:hi>; nor shall those only be rewarded, who give them great Entertainments, and make them great Presents, but (if it be proportionable to what they are able to do) tho it be a kindness of the mo<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t Minute Consideration, but a <ns0:hi>Cup of Cold Water,</ns0:hi> they shall be reward<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed. God rewards the love we shew to him and the good Acti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ons, that flow from it. Here are three Persons mentioned, for whose <ns0:hi>Entertainment,</ns0:hi> and reception, God hath provided in this Promise. A <ns0:hi>Prophet.</ns0:hi> A <ns0:hi>Righteous Man,</ns0:hi> a <ns0:hi>little one.</ns0:hi> And a three-fold reward promised. <ns0:hi>The reward of a Prophet. The reward of a Righteous Man, and his reward.</ns0:hi> How to di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stinguish the <ns0:hi>Righteous Man,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>little one,</ns0:hi> I cannot tell, unless we understand by the <ns0:hi>Righteous man,</ns0:hi> one more <ns0:hi>per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fect,</ns0:hi> more Eminent in holiness, and by the <ns0:hi>little one,</ns0:hi> one that is <ns0:hi>sincere,</ns0:hi> tho we cannot Judge him so grown in Grace, and the knowledge of Christ. I should understand no more by the <ns0:hi>three-fold rewards,</ns0:hi> then Gods more particular Value for his Ministers, and for such as are more perfect in Holiness. While in the mean time he will not <ns0:hi>break the bruised Reed, nor quench the smoaking Flax,</ns0:hi> and that every one shall be re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />warded according to his Works. Which shall not be measured by the quantity of the Gift, but by the Obedience, and Affection, and Ability of the giver; <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 21.2, 3. <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 6.1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
            </ns0:div>
